newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FINAL ROUND OF TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP POSTPONED.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FINAL ROUND OF TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP POSTPONED.

text.p: Tom Lehman will have to wait another day before taking advantage of his enormous lead at the $3 million Tour Championship after the final round was postponed until Monday by drenching rain on Sunday.

Nearly two inches (5 cm) of rain fell on Southern Hills Sunday morning, scattering deep puddles around the course and washing out almost every bunker ahead of the final 18 holes of the season finale for only the year's top 30 money winners.
Lehman, at 13-under-par, held a nine-stroke lead after 54 holes -- the largest advantage on the PGA Tour since Jack Nicklaus in 1973.
But even with the outcome a likely foregone conclusion, Lehman was all in favour of postponing the final round rather than shortening the tournament and declaring him the winner.
"I think the tour made the right decision," Lehman said.

"Anytime you win a tournament that's been shortened because of weather it lacks a little finality. Part of winning, actually, is sleeping on a lead and going out and having to play to win the next day."
With his likely victory on Monday, barring a final-round collapse that would dwarf even Greg Norman's Master's fade, Lehman will strengthen his chances of landing PGA Player of the Year honours.
Lehman, the British Open champion, can also lock up the Vardon Trophy for the season's low scoring average with a decent showing on Monday.
Phil Mickelson, currently in a tie for seventh and another leading Player of the Year candidate, must finish second or third to remain in first place on the 1996 money list.
PGA Tour Commissioner Tim Finchem said officials decided this was too big an event to shorten it to 54 holes.
"This is an important championship, it's the end of the season, there are a number of individual matters riding on the outcome of this event, and it is a substantial purse," Finchem pointed out.
"We felt that it was important to give our best effort to carry it to 72 holes."
